dataModel.title: Data structure
dataModel.subtitle: How this system stores its data. Structure only: no real records are shown here.
dataModel.link: About this system: how data is stored
dataModel.p1: Each board row, client, entity and task has core columns that business logic depends on. Every other field is a custom field: its value sits in that record's data column, under the field's key.
dataModel.p2: Field, status and role keys never change once created; only labels do. Imports, automations and views refer to keys.
dataModel.p3: Facts about a client (portal access, ABN, address, contact) are stored once on the client and shown on boards as mirror columns.
dataModel.p4: Every change goes through one write path: it is logged in command_log, its before/after values go to audit_entries, and an event is queued for automations and notifications.
dataModel.p5: Deleting is soft: deleted_at is set and the record disappears from screens, but it can be restored from activity.
dataModel.fieldsIntro: Fields configured for each product line, and where their values are kept. Only product lines you can open are listed.
dataModel.label: Label

tables.workspaces: Product lines (Accounting, Grants). Settings hold core column labels, auto-fill rules and the roll-over default.
tables.workspace_memberships: A user's role in a product line: viewer, member, manager or admin.
tables.boards: Boards. A board can be linked to a fiscal year; settings list the statuses and fields it uses.
tables.field_definitions: Custom field definitions. entity_kind says what they belong to (item, task, client, entity, contact). The key never changes.
tables.statuses: Status options with colour and category (todo, active, waiting, done, cancelled), for items or tasks.
tables.member_roles: Team roles people can hold on a row (Preparer, Manager, Partner, Responsible Person…).
tables.lookup_lists: Managed master-data lists such as Software or Company.
tables.lookup_values: Values of a master-data list; can be deactivated and have aliases.
tables.clients: Clients. data holds client-level custom fields (portal access, address, communication…).
tables.client_entities: Legal or tax entities under a client: type, ABN, ACN, year end, primary flag.
tables.contacts: Contacts of a client; can be marked primary, billing or referrer.
tables.items: One row on a board. Core columns hold what business logic needs; everything else is in data.
tables.item_members: Who holds which role on a row, and when they were assigned.
tables.tasks: Tasks under a row; can be nested.
tables.saved_views: Saved columns, filters, sorting and search; personal or shared.
tables.comments: Updates and comments on rows, clients or tasks; mentions lists who was @-ed.
tables.automation_rules: Automation rules: trigger, conditions and actions.
tables.automation_runs: Each time a rule ran. What it changed is read from the audit trail.
tables.users: People. Placeholder users (from old short names) can later get an email and password.
tables.auth_sessions: Login sessions. Only a hash of the token is stored.
tables.login_attempts: Login attempts, used for rate limiting.
tables.migration_runs: Import batches from CSV or ERPNext.
tables.migration_rows: Each source row of an import, staged with its issues.
tables.external_refs: Mapping from old-system IDs to new records, so re-importing does not duplicate.
tables.command_log: Every write: who, what, from where, result, duration, idempotency key.
tables.audit_entries: One row per changed object with field-level before and after values. Activity, undo and rollback read it.
tables.events: Event outbox: something happened (row created, field changed…).
tables.event_deliveries: Delivery state of each event to each subscriber.
tables.files: Uploaded files attached to an item or client. Old versions are kept because citations point at the exact version.
tables.file_versions: Each uploaded version of a file: storage key, size, checksum and who uploaded it.
tables.ai_calls: Every AI model call: task, provider and model, client whose data was sent, tokens and result.
tables.rdti_activities: R&D activities of a Grants project: core or supporting (a supporting one points at a core one).
tables.rdti_chunks: Citable passages extracted from evidence files, with page and position, optionally assigned to an activity.
tables.rdti_assessments: How well the evidence covers each RDTI element of an activity (sufficient, partial, missing), by AI or a person.
tables.rdti_checklist_items: Items to request from the client to fill evidence gaps: preferred document, alternatives, example, status.
tables.rdti_report_sections: Report sections per activity and element. Locked sections are not regenerated or edited.
tables.rdti_claims: Statements inside a report section, with their review status (sourced, needs review, our wording, no source).
tables.rdti_citations: The source passage and exact quote behind a statement, whether the quote was found, and how well it supports it.
